bluf: Adapt Worldwide is a UK based, enterprise facing performance media agency and Welo Global brand buying international paid media and localising content for global brands. It leads with paid search behind Google Premier Partner 2025 and Microsoft Advertising Elite Partner 2024 badges and positions AI across every line without an audited product. The record points nowhere: one undated holdco move, no news, no jobs, a sitemap with 0 updates in 365 days. A rival should know that it headlines LinkedIn ABM for Panasonic Toughbook while the LinkedIn Ad Library shows 0 ads of its own, and that all 20 clients on record are names without described work.
doing:
Adapt Worldwide sells itself as a multilingual, performance led agency and a Welo Global brand combining international paid media, AI and localised content so global brands perform in every market: it buys media across borders for large companies and localises the content that goes with it. Its headline claim is two named jobs: global analytics tracking built across Grant Thornton's 90 websites, and LinkedIn ABM lead generation run across Europe for Panasonic Toughbook.

The sold mix leads with paid search, scored 3 and the only lead line; SEO, paid social, data and measurement, and B2B and ABM are core at 2 each. Behind the lead line sit an International Paid Media pillar, the Google Premier Partner 2025 and Microsoft Advertising Elite Partner 2024 badges, and the Rooster Money paid search case. Partners listed: Google Marketing Platform certification, Meta Business Partner, LinkedIn Marketing Partner. Two proprietary lines: Adapt Studio, a content production unit, and Adapt x AI, an AI offer that exists as a navigation label. Programmatic and CTV, retail media and CRO score 1 with no evidence note; email and CRM, creator, local and web build score 0.

Its AI posture is broad and thin: AI powered media buying, AI driven localisation, an AI SEO service framed as GEO and the Adapt x AI line, with the AI search capability scored 1 and no evidence note. Moves: one, undated: the About page now presents Adapt as a Welo Global brand, deal timing not shown. The record holds no news, no case study text, no job listings and no pricing signals. Conspicuously absent for a shop of its kind: an office list, a founding year, an employee count, any case study with described results, and a publishing cadence (537 sitemap URLs, 0 updated in 90 days, 0 in 365). The live site returned 403 to the crawler and the record was scored from a May 2026 Internet Archive capture.
clients:
The record's client type is enterprise; verticals list SaaS, logistics, manufacturing, ecommerce, travel, technology and financial services. The home market is the UK by headquarters, with specialists spread across countries per the About page and no office list.

The needs read holds 20 clients, 0 with an observed need and 20 named only; evidence types split as case study 5, case study by slug 8 and client logo 7. The capability notes describe the work for some case study clients: NatWest Rooster Money came for paid performance (the Rooster Money paid search case); Panasonic (Toughbook) came for B2B pipeline (the LinkedIn ABM case across Europe); Oak Tree Mobility came for local and lead generation (the Oak Tree lead generation case); Grant Thornton came for data and measurement (global tracking across its 90 websites). ShipStation has a case study page with no described work, so its need is inferred from the paid search lead. The slug only names are Vue Cinemas, National Trust, Hearst, Tes, Meyer Group, BAM Bamboo Clothing, Saltrock and Oak Furniture Superstore, needs inferred from the sold mix. The logo wall names Uber, Spotify, Booking, LinkedIn, Kuehne + Nagel, Neogen Corporation and Intrepid with no work described.

The shared read finds 2 of the book on other tracked books: Uber with moburst and Spotify with instrument.

What the base needs next: KJ1 (the click is being replaced by the citation) and KJ4 (the platforms are absorbing the execution layer) bear hardest on an enterprise book bought on cross border paid media. It is likely, moderate confidence, that these clients will ask for citation and AI answer measurement alongside paid search reporting, and likely that platform automation will take the hours the paid lines bill; the Grant Thornton tracking work is its one measurement proof point.
house: Say and do: two lines tested, one practised. Paid search is corroborated: it runs its own Google ads, 6 in the Transparency Center and 1 in the last 30 days, last shown 2026-09-26, with the advertiser record naming Search Star Ltd and no sample text on record. LinkedIn advertising is contradicted: it sells paid social and B2B demand generation and the Ad Library returns 0 ads (the note reads '0 ads match the name query (all advertisers); first results page shows 0 cards'). Paid social is unknown, no pixel detected. Publishing cadence was not measured, but the sitemap lists 537 URLs with 0 updated in 90 days, 0 in 365 days and 0 AI URLs. The tag stack is GTM alone on WordPress: no social pixels, no test tools, no ABM stack. The record holds no llms.txt reading, lists no AI crawlers blocked, and holds no Meta or TikTok reading. The one flagged gap is the LinkedIn contradiction.
market:
The Horus read puts Adapt Worldwide at a tailwind index of -12.3, band Exposed, percentile 6, 17:01 on the Solar Arc, dusk (Atum). Best placed for KJ1 (the click replaced by the citation, driven by AI Search / GEO) and KJ2 (ads inside AI answers). Most exposed to KJ6 (the agency middle hollowed out, driven by Paid Search, Paid Social and SEO) and KJ4 (platforms absorbing the execution layer). Best scenario fit: The Walled Oasis, 41/100. It is making P4 (supplying the inputs automation runs on), partial on P1, absent on P2, P6, P7 and P8; P3 does not apply, P5 unknown.

The Monsoon read is 50.2, band Breeze, percentile 29: migration 57.7 against displacement 42.7. The sold mix supplies 48 of the index, SEO (11) and Paid Search (11) carrying the most movable hours; the work would go 65% to South and Southeast Asia, 20% to Eastern Europe and 15% to Africa and the Maghreb, and automation overlaps 31% of it. The footprint is inferred: no hub offices and no onshore claims in the record.
openings:
The strongest opening is the LinkedIn contradiction: the headline claim is LinkedIn ABM lead generation for Panasonic Toughbook across Europe and the Ad Library shows 0 ads under its name. A rival selling B2B pipeline to the SaaS, logistics and manufacturing accounts it names can very likely (high confidence) lead with a running LinkedIn programme. Falsifier: a later compile showing company or thought leader ads under the Adapt Worldwide name closes this opening.

The book is contestable because it is thin: 20 of 20 clients are names without described work, and Uber and Spotify sit with moburst and instrument. Ask about the logo wall names; it is likely, moderate confidence, that some are past or partial engagements.

It sells AI SEO as GEO with no audited AI visibility product (P1 partial) and no feed, schema or entity work (P2 absent): a rival with a citation share scorecard leads with the number. No sign of ads tested inside AI assistants (P8 absent), no public pricing model (P5). Displacement at 42.7 says the book does not buy on price, so the pitch is proof, not rate. The idle sitemap (0 updates in 90 days) is the symptom to raise.
watch: I8, holdco Q3 organic growth, headcount and pricing model disclosures, next reading October 2026: output or outcome pricing announced at a top five holdco would deepen the KJ6 exposure of a Welo Global brand with no public pricing.

I2, Alphabet Q3 2026 search growth and AI Mode ad disclosures, late October 2026: growth below 10% flags cannibalization of the paid search lead line, above 15% with AI Mode ads live confirms S1 and the KJ1 tailwind.
I10, Reddit US daily users against search referral volatility, late October 2026: US DAUq growth at or below 5% alongside AI Mode growth confirms the UGC starvation risk under KJ1.
I3, OpenAI ad run rate disclosures and CPM trend, rolling: the next milestone ($2B) and pricing below $20 CPM would say whether the KJ2 tailwind arrives before the P8 gap closes.

The undated Welo Global move: the About page presents Adapt as a Welo Global brand with no deal timing shown, so the next compile should look for the date, an office list and whether its Google ads resume after the 2026-09-26 last shown date.
